title: Examining Pre-service Mathematics Teachers' Purposes of Using ChatGPT in Lesson Plan Development
extended_summary:
This paper examines why pre-service middle school mathematics teachers used ChatGPT while developing lesson plans. The study asks how ChatGPT supported lesson content creation and how it helped participants deepen their own knowledge and address gaps while planning instruction.

The intervention/approach studied was the use of ChatGPT as an AI tool during lesson plan development. Participants were 56 third-year pre-service middle school mathematics teachers enrolled at a state university in Turkey. They were asked to select mathematics curriculum outcomes, prepare a lesson plan using ChatGPT, and then respond to an open-ended questionnaire. The analysis used qualitative content analysis.

Findings showed that ChatGPT was used most often to create lesson content: generating learning activities, problems and examples, assessment tools, course flow, creative ideas, explanations of math concepts, interdisciplinary and real-life connections, and revisions to lesson plans. A second major use was helping participants deepen pedagogical knowledge and fill conceptual gaps, especially around teaching strategies, materials, classroom management, and mathematical concepts. The paper concludes that ChatGPT can be a useful support tool in teacher education, but it should complement rather than replace teachers' own expertise, and its outputs should be checked for accuracy.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative phenomenological study using open-ended questionnaire responses from 56 pre-service teachers, with content analysis and interrater agreement reported. It is peer-reviewed and methodologically clear, but it does not provide experimental or causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived benefits for lesson planning and teacher knowledge, but no quantitative impact on student outcomes or workload reduction is measured. The likely impact is positive yet modest and unclear in magnitude because findings are descriptive and self-reported.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used by pre-service middle school mathematics teachers to support lesson plan development, including generating learning activities, problems/examples, evaluation tools, course flow, concept explanations, and revision suggestions.

finding.finding_summary: This qualitative phenomenology study (n=56 pre-service middle school mathematics teachers) found that ChatGPT was used extensively to support mathematics lesson planning, especially for explaining concepts, generating problems and examples, and structuring lesson flow. The paper does not report effect sizes, but participants consistently described ChatGPT as helpful for deepening mathematical content understanding and improving the quality of math instruction materials.
finding.measure: Self-reported purposes and uses of ChatGPT during mathematics lesson plan development; content analysis of open-ended questionnaire responses

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported that ChatGPT supported creative thinking, idea generation, and connecting mathematical concepts to daily life, other lessons, and prior knowledge. It also helped some pre-service teachers deepen pedagogical knowledge and identify gaps in their own understanding, suggesting benefits for metacognition and instructional planning rather than direct student achievement.
finding.measure: Self-reported uses of ChatGPT for creativity, conceptual linking, and knowledge deepening in lesson planning

finding.finding_summary: The paper indicates that ChatGPT improved efficiency in lesson planning by helping participants rapidly produce course flow, assessment ideas, activities, and revised lesson materials. Teachers described it as saving time and reducing effort in planning and editing, but the study provides no quantitative workload estimates or effect sizes.
finding.measure: Self-reported lesson-planning productivity and editing support
